extracted.intended_audience: researchers using or planning to apply for Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) / JSPS applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and applicant-facing standards for Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI), describing the program purpose, eligible fields, selection process, and applicant resources. Intended to guide researchers who will apply for or manage KAKENHI funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research are competitive research funds that are intended to significantly develop all scientific research (research based on the free ideas of the researcher), from basic to applied research in all fields, ranging from the humanities and the social sciences to the natural sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program supports creative and pioneering research projects expected to become the foundation of social development. Applicants should propose research grounded in the researcher's own free ideas and aiming for significant development of their field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of eligible fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicable to 'all fields, ranging from the humanities and the social sciences to the natural sciences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KAKENHI covers a broad disciplinary span; applicants from any academic field may apply under appropriate research categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive nature of funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research are competitive research funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect competition for awards; proposals are evaluated against other submissions and limited budgetary resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection method — peer-review screening
rubrics_metrics.description: The research projects are selected using a peer-review screening process (screening by multiple researchers whose field of specialization is close to that of the applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals will be reviewed by several specialists in closely related fields; clarity, alignment with disciplinary standards, and convincing justification of significance and methods are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to publish research results
rubrics_metrics.description: Research results obtained under these Grants-in-Aid are widely published in academic journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful projects are expected to produce publishable outputs; applicants should plan for dissemination of findings in peer-reviewed venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program categories and guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'Types of Grants Programs', 'KAKENHI pamphlet', and 'Handbook for Researchers' as primary explanatory resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the listed materials (pamphlet, Handbook for Researchers) to determine the purposes and descriptions of each research category, application procedures, and specific requirements (including multi-year fund information and abstracts of large-scale projects). The Handbook is prepared primarily for researchers using or planning to apply and provides simple descriptions of the basic contents of the grant program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information resources & transparency (award trends, archives)
rubrics_metrics.description: The site provides 'Peer Review Process', 'Award Trends', 'Research Results Database & Archives', and 'Abstracts of Large-scale Research Projects' to inform applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can and should review past award trends and abstracts to understand standards of successful proposals and expected project scale; transparency resources can inform competitive positioning and proposal design.
